operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Executive Order 10750, signed 1958-01-28, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between Eastern Air Lines, Inc., and employees represented by the Air Line Pilots Association, International. Its single paragraph carries three commands that belong to one procedure: creation of the board ("hereby create a board of"), the direction that the board report to the President ("within thirty days from the date"), and the status-quo rule that, from the order’s date and for thirty days after the report, no change in the conditions out of which the dispute arose is to be made except by agreement ("thirty days after the Board"). The order has no termination clause, fixed end date or revocation clause of its own. The thirty-day report date and the end of the thirty-day period after the report are spent facts and not ends. The held NMB report text for this board (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10750_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10750_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_c69ca7f6fc.txt) gives the date 1958-07-21 on its cover and letter of transmittal; a dated transmittal letter is not proof of the day the President received the report, so this is a disclosed spent fact and not an end. If the report was made on 1958-07-21, the thirty-day period after the report ran through 1958-08-20, and the order was functionally spent on 1958-08-20 (owner ruling research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-report-deadline.md, both dates recorded). First end: Executive Order 12553, signed 1986-02-25, revokes this order by number. The cited source is the enacting sentence of EO 12553, which says "longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" The dossier records an agent-located acting provision for this pair that an independent AI review upheld (a hypothesis, not a certification). The table in EO 12553 (page 11 of the held Federal Register text) lists the number 10750 at character offset 10644 as entry 44 of 64; the text layer prints the 64 numbers first and the 64 subjects afterwards, and entry 44 of the subject list is the subject Creating an emergency board to investigate an airline labor dispute, which agrees with this order’s own title. The alignment is by position, not by a printed row, and a reviewer should confirm it. EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording of its own (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become and similar words), so the date it was signed, 1986-02-25, is recorded as the end date. The held text also shows the filing date 1986-02-26 and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03; those are the alternative readings and none of them changes the conclusion that the order was no longer in force after 1986-03-03.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Executive Order 10757, signed 1958-02-27, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between seven airlines (Eastern, Trans World, United, Northwest, Northeast, Capital and National) and employees represented by the International Association of Machinists. Its single paragraph carries three commands that belong to one procedure: creation of the board ("hereby create a board"), the direction that the board report to the President ("within thirty days from the date"), and the status-quo rule that, from the order’s date and for thirty days after the report, no change in the conditions out of which the dispute arose is to be made except by agreement ("except by agreement"). The order has no termination clause, fixed end date or revocation clause of its own. The thirty-day report date and the end of the thirty-day period after the report are spent facts and not ends. The held NMB report text for this board (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10757_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10757_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_22203830f5.txt) gives the date 1958-09-15 on its cover and letter of transmittal; a dated transmittal letter is not proof of the day the President received the report, so this is a disclosed spent fact and not an end. If the report was made on 1958-09-15, the thirty-day period after the report ran through 1958-10-15, and the order was functionally spent on 1958-10-15 (owner ruling research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-report-deadline.md, both dates recorded). First end: Executive Order 12553, signed 1986-02-25, revokes this order by number. The cited source is the enacting sentence of EO 12553, which says "longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" The dossier records an agent-located acting provision for this pair that an independent AI review upheld (a hypothesis, not a certification). The table in EO 12553 (page 11 of the held Federal Register text) lists the number 10757 at character offset 10651 as entry 45 of 64; the text layer prints the 64 numbers first and the 64 subjects afterwards, and entry 45 of the subject list is the subject Creating an emergency board to investigate an airline labor dispute, which agrees with this order’s own title. The alignment is by position, not by a printed row, and a reviewer should confirm it. EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording of its own (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become and similar words), so the date it was signed, 1986-02-25, is recorded as the end date. The held text also shows the filing date 1986-02-26 and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03; those are the alternative readings and none of them changes the conclusion that the order was no longer in force after 1986-03-03.

research_rationale:
EO 10760 is a Railway Labor Act section 10 emergency-board order with provisional status no. I read the held registered Federal Register text, confirmed the order’s identity from its heading and number, and confirmed a single-clause inventory. It has no own-terms end. The only held instrument that revokes it is EO 12553 (1986-02-25), which I read; the report date and the end of the status-quo period are disclosed spent facts, not ends. The searches chosen (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) carry no coverage warning and show no hit for this order that contradicts the ending.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Searched for an end earlier than 1986-02-25. The order’s own terms contain only the report direction and the status-quo period, which are report-relative deadlines and not ends. The Cruden number lookup in LOOKUPS.md finds this number cited only in the order’s own held texts, in the NMB report text where one is held, and in EO 12553 (and, for EO 10760, in the Federal Register page of EO 10761, where only the page listing cites it and no change provision exists). No held later order other than EO 12553 revokes, supersedes, amends or terminates it, and no statute held in the packet does so; an unnamed statute or order would in any case not end it (owner ruling 2026-10-21 unnamed instruments). The dossier’s conflicts and missing lists are empty or concern only a number citation without a change provision (report dated 1958-07-25 in the held NMB text; thirty days later is 1958-08-24).","independent_command_check":"No independent command survives: the board’s creation was performed when the order issued; the report direction and the status-quo period are time-limited by the order itself and by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act; the order creates no standing office, delegation, rule or continuing duty that would outlast the report and the thirty-day period. Those spent commands nonetheless remained formally in the order until EO 12553, and the order is recorded as ending on revocation under the owner’s report-deadline ruling.","savings_check":"EO 12553 has no saving, exception or pending-matters language: a search of the whole held text for except, notwithstanding, nothing in, saving, pending and similar words found only incidental uses inside other orders’ subject lines. The board’s report and any agreement or later change in working conditions between the parties are accrued consequences that rest on the Railway Labor Act and the parties’ own acts, not on this order, and none keeps the order operative.","scope_check":"The whole order is covered: EO 12553 revokes listed orders \"and any amendments thereto\" with no exception, so no part of this one-paragraph order was left in force. The clause inventory is one clause (the whole order); I read the held text and confirm that it contains the creation, report and status-quo commands and nothing else operative."}

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Executive Order 10770, signed 1958-06-19, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between American Airlines, Incorporated, and employees represented by the Air Line Pilots Association, International. Its single paragraph carries three commands that belong to one procedure: creation of the board ("hereby create a board"), the direction that the board report to the President ("within thirty days from the date"), and the status-quo rule that, from the order’s date and for thirty days after the report, no change in the conditions out of which the dispute arose is to be made except by agreement ("except by agreement"). The order has no termination clause, fixed end date or revocation clause of its own. The thirty-day report date and the end of the thirty-day period after the report are spent facts and not ends. No held text gives the actual date of this board’s report, so neither the report date nor the end of the thirty-day period after it is established from held evidence; the claim does not depend on them because a report deadline and a status-quo period are not ends (owner ruling research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-report-deadline.md). First end: Executive Order 12553, signed 1986-02-25, revokes this order by number. The dossier holds no located acting-provision record for this pair, so the cited source is the whole held Federal Register text of EO 12553 (the dossier’s actor context); its enacting sentence says "longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" The table in EO 12553 (page 11 of the held Federal Register text) lists the number 10770 at character offset 10665 as entry 47 of 64; the text layer prints the 64 numbers first and the 64 subjects afterwards, and entry 47 of the subject list is the subject Creating an emergency board to investigate an airline labor dispute, which agrees with this order’s own title. The alignment is by position, not by a printed row, and a reviewer should confirm it. EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording of its own (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become and similar words), so the date it was signed, 1986-02-25, is recorded as the end date. The held text also shows the filing date 1986-02-26 and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03; those are the alternative readings and none of them changes the conclusion that the order was no longer in force after 1986-03-03.

EO 10770 is a Railway Labor Act section 10 emergency-board order with provisional status no. I read the held registered Federal Register text, confirmed the order’s identity from its heading and number, and confirmed a single-clause inventory. It has no own-terms end. The only held instrument that revokes it is EO 12553 (1986-02-25), which I read; the report date and the end of the status-quo period are disclosed spent facts, not ends. The searches chosen (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) carry no coverage warning and show no hit for this order that contradicts the ending.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Searched for an end earlier than 1986-02-25. The order’s own terms contain only the report direction and the status-quo period, which are report-relative deadlines and not ends. The Cruden number lookup in LOOKUPS.md finds this number cited only in the order’s own held texts, in the NMB report text where one is held, and in EO 12553. No held later order other than EO 12553 revokes, supersedes, amends or terminates it, and no statute held in the packet does so; an unnamed statute or order would in any case not end it (owner ruling 2026-10-21 unnamed instruments). The dossier’s conflicts and missing lists are empty or concern only a number citation without a change provision (no held text gives the actual report date).","independent_command_check":"No independent command survives: the board’s creation was performed when the order issued; the report direction and the status-quo period are time-limited by the order itself and by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act; the order creates no standing office, delegation, rule or continuing duty that would outlast the report and the thirty-day period. Those spent commands nonetheless remained formally in the order until EO 12553, and the order is recorded as ending on revocation under the owner’s report-deadline ruling.","savings_check":"EO 12553 has no saving, exception or pending-matters language: a search of the whole held text for except, notwithstanding, nothing in, saving, pending and similar words found only incidental uses inside other orders’ subject lines. The board’s report and any agreement or later change in working conditions between the parties are accrued consequences that rest on the Railway Labor Act and the parties’ own acts, not on this order, and none keeps the order operative.","scope_check":"The whole order is covered: EO 12553 revokes listed orders \"and any amendments thereto\" with no exception, so no part of this one-paragraph order was left in force. The clause inventory is one clause (the whole order); I read the held text and confirm that it contains the creation, report and status-quo commands and nothing else operative."}

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Executive Order 10862, signed 1960-02-12, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between the Atchison, Topeka and Santa Fe Railway Company--Coast Lines and certain of its employees. Its single paragraph carries three commands that belong to one procedure: creation of the board ("hereby create a board of"), the direction that the board report to the President ("within thirty days from the date"), and the status-quo rule that, from the order’s date and for thirty days after the report, no change in the conditions out of which the dispute arose is to be made except by agreement ("except by agreement"). The order has no termination clause, fixed end date or revocation clause of its own. The thirty-day report date and the end of the thirty-day period after the report are spent facts and not ends. The held NMB report text for this board (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10862_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10862_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_e38f8f604e.txt) gives the date 1960-07-15 on its cover (the letter of transmittal’s year is misread by the text layer as 1980, an apparent recognition error); a dated transmittal letter is not proof of the day the President received the report, so this is a disclosed spent fact and not an end. If the report was made on 1960-07-15, the thirty-day period after the report ran through 1960-08-14, and the order was functionally spent on 1960-08-14 (owner ruling research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-report-deadline.md, both dates recorded). First end: Executive Order 12553, signed 1986-02-25, revokes this order by number. The cited source is the enacting sentence of EO 12553, which says "longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" The dossier records an agent-located acting provision for this pair that an independent AI review upheld (a hypothesis, not a certification). The table in EO 12553 (page 11 of the held Federal Register text) lists the number 10862 at character offset 10715 as entry 55 of 64; the text layer prints the 64 numbers first and the 64 subjects afterwards, and entry 55 of the subject list is the subject Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute, which agrees with this order’s own title. The alignment is by position, not by a printed row, and a reviewer should confirm it. EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording of its own (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become and similar words), so the date it was signed, 1986-02-25, is recorded as the end date. The held text also shows the filing date 1986-02-26 and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03; those are the alternative readings and none of them changes the conclusion that the order was no longer in force after 1986-03-03.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Executive Order 10862
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD  
TO INVESTIGATE A DISPUTE BE­
TWEEN THE ATCHISON, TOPEKA  
AND SANTA FE RAILWAY COM­
PANY— COAST LINES AND CER­
TAIN OF ITS EMPLOYEES
WHEREAS a dispute exists between  
the Atchison, Topeka and Santa Fe Rail­
way Company— Coast Lines, a carrier,  
and certain of its employees represented 
by the Brotherhood of Locomotive En­
gineers, a labor organization; and
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provi­
sions of the Railway Labor Act, as  
amended; and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board,  
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as to  
deprive a section of the country of es­
sential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the  
authority vested in me by section 10 of  
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45  
U.S.C. 160), I hereby create a board of  
three members, to be appointed by me,  
to investigate this dispute. No member  
of the board shall be pecuniarily or  
otherwise interested in any organization  
of railway employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to  
the President with respect to the dispute  
within thirty days from the date of this  
order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this  
date and for thirty days after the board  
has made its report to the President, no  
change, except by agreement, shall be  
made by the Atchison, Topeka and Santa  
Fe Railway Company— Coast Lines, or by 
its employees, in the conditions out of  
which the dispute arose.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Executive Order 10868, signed 1960-02-29, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between the New York Central System and certain of its employees. Its single paragraph carries three commands that belong to one procedure: creation of the board ("hereby create a board of"), the direction that the board report to the President ("within thirty days from the date"), and the status-quo rule that, from the order’s date and for thirty days after the report, no change in the conditions out of which the dispute arose is to be made except by agreement ("except by agreement"). The order has no termination clause, fixed end date or revocation clause of its own. The thirty-day report date and the end of the thirty-day period after the report are spent facts and not ends. The held NMB report text for this board (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10868_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10868_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_fc0ec43545.txt) gives the date 1960-06-20 on its cover and letter of transmittal; a dated transmittal letter is not proof of the day the President received the report, so this is a disclosed spent fact and not an end. If the report was made on 1960-06-20, the thirty-day period after the report ran through 1960-07-20, and the order was functionally spent on 1960-07-20 (owner ruling research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-report-deadline.md, both dates recorded). First end: Executive Order 12553, signed 1986-02-25, revokes this order by number. The cited source is the enacting sentence of EO 12553, which says "longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" The dossier records an agent-located acting provision for this pair that an independent AI review upheld (a hypothesis, not a certification). The table in EO 12553 (page 11 of the held Federal Register text) lists the number 10868 at character offset 10721 as entry 56 of 64; the text layer prints the 64 numbers first and the 64 subjects afterwards, and entry 56 of the subject list is the subject Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute, which agrees with this order’s own title. The alignment is by position, not by a printed row, and a reviewer should confirm it. EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording of its own (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become and similar words), so the date it was signed, 1986-02-25, is recorded as the end date. The held text also shows the filing date 1986-02-26 and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03; those are the alternative readings and none of them changes the conclusion that the order was no longer in force after 1986-03-03.

Executive Order 10868
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD  
TO INVESTIGATE A DISPUTE BE­
TWEEN THE NEW YORK CENTRAL  
SYSTEM AND CERTAIN OF ITS  
EMPLOYEES
WHEREAS a dispute exists between  
the New York Central System, a carrier,  
and certain of its employees represented  
by the Order of Railway Conductors and  
Brakemen, a labor organization; and  
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provi­
sions of the Railway Labor Act, as  
amended; and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the' National Mediation Board,  
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as to  
deprive a section of the country of essen­
tial transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the  
authority vested in me by section 10 of  
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45  
U.S.C. 160), I hereby create a board of  
three members, to be appointed by me,  
to investigate this dispute. No member  
of the board shall be pecuniarily or  
otherwise interested in any organization  
of railway employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to  
the President with respect to the dispute  
within thirty days from the date of this  
order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this  
date and for thirty days after the board  
has made its report to the President, no  
change, except by agreement, shall be  
made by the New York Central System,  
or by its employees, in the conditions out  
of which the dispute arose.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Executive Order 10877, signed 1960-05-20, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between the Pennsylvania Railroad Company and certain of its employees. Its single paragraph carries three commands that belong to one procedure: creation of the board ("hereby create a board of"), the direction that the board report to the President ("within thirty days from the date"), and the status-quo rule that, from the order’s date and for thirty days after the report, no change in the conditions out of which the dispute arose is to be made except by agreement ("except by agreement"). The order has no termination clause, fixed end date or revocation clause of its own. The thirty-day report date and the end of the thirty-day period after the report are spent facts and not ends. No held text gives the actual date of this board’s report, so neither the report date nor the end of the thirty-day period after it is established from held evidence; the claim does not depend on them because a report deadline and a status-quo period are not ends (owner ruling research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-report-deadline.md). First end: Executive Order 12553, signed 1986-02-25, revokes this order by number. The dossier holds no located acting-provision record for this pair, so the cited source is the whole held Federal Register text of EO 12553 (the dossier’s actor context); its enacting sentence says "longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" The table in EO 12553 (page 11 of the held Federal Register text) lists the number 10877 at character offset 10745 as entry 60 of 64; the text layer prints the 64 numbers first and the 64 subjects afterwards, and entry 60 of the subject list is the subject Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute, which agrees with this order’s own title. The alignment is by position, not by a printed row, and a reviewer should confirm it. EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording of its own (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become and similar words), so the date it was signed, 1986-02-25, is recorded as the end date. The held text also shows the filing date 1986-02-26 and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03; those are the alternative readings and none of them changes the conclusion that the order was no longer in force after 1986-03-03.

Executive Order 10877
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD  
TO INVESTIGATE A DISPUTE BE­
TWEEN THE PENNSYLVANIA RAIL­
ROAD COMPANY AND CERTAIN  
OF ITS EMPLOYEES
WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
the Pennsylvania Railroad Company, a 
carrier, and certain of its employees 
represented by the Transport Workers’ 
Union of America, Railroad Division, 
AFL-CIO, and System Federation No. 
152, Railway Employes’ Department, 
AFL-CIO, labor organizations; and 
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the pro­
visions of the Railway Labor Act, as 
amended; and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as to 
deprive a section of the country of es­
sential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U.S.C. 160), I  hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, 
to investigate this dispute. No member 
of the board shall be pecuniarily or 
otherwise interested in any organization 
of railroad employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the dispute 
within thirty days from the date of this 
order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way -Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by the Pennsylvania Railroad 
Company, or by its employees, in the 
conditions out of which the dispute 
arose.,

§ 421.5340 Bagged and bulk rice.
Rice may be either in bags or in bulk 
when a loan is obtained or when rice 
is purchased under a purchase agree­
ment.
(a) Farm  storage.  (1) Loans on farm - 
stored rice will be made on a bagged or 
bulk basis in accordance with the manner 
in which the rice is stored.
(2) Settlement with respect to farm - 
stored rice acquired by CCC in bulk under 
loan or purchase agreement shall be on 
the basis of the net weight of the bulk 
rice acquired by CCC.
(3) Settlement with respect to farm - 
stored rice acquired by CCC in bags 
under loan or purchase agreement shall 
be on the basis of the combined weight 
of the rice and bags acquired by CCC, 
and title to the bags shall pass with the 
rice. CCC shall not otherwise pay any 
amounts representing the value of the 
bags.
(b) Approved w arehouse storage.  (1) 
In  the case of rice in approved ware­
house storage, loans shall be made and 
rice under purchase agreement shall be 
acquired on a bagged or bulk basis in 
accordance with the manner in which 
the rice is to be loaded out by the ware­
houseman as indicated on the warehouse 
receipt. Therefore, if a loan is made on 
the basis of loading out the rice in bags, 
the rice must be in bags at the time of 
load out by the warehouseman and, if 
a loan is made on the basis of loading out 
the rice in bulk, the rice must be in bulk 
at the time of load out by the warehouse­
man.
(2) Settlement with respect to rice in 
approved warehouse storage acquired by 
CCC under loans or purchase agree­
ments, which the warehouseman is re­
quired to load out in bulk shall be on 
the basis of the net weight of bulk rice 
acquired by CCC under loan or purchase 
agreements.
(3) Settlement with respect to rice in 
approved warehouse storage, acquired by 
CCC under loans or purchase agree­
ments, which the warehouseman is re­
quired to load out in bags shall be on 
the basis of the combined weight of the 
rice and bags, and title to the bags shall 
pass with the rice, except that, if the 
rice is not in bags at the time of acqui­
sition by CCC title to the bags shall pass 
to CCC at the time of load out. CCC 
shall not otherwise pay any amounts 
representing the value of the bags. In 
the event any person should successfully 
dispute the passing of title to the bags, 
the producer shall indemnify CCC for 
any loss sustained by reason thereof.
§  421.5341 Warehouse receipts.
(a) Warehouse receipts must be is­
sued in the name of the producer, or 
cooperative marketing association, must 
be properly endorsed in blank so as to 
vest title in any holder, and must be 
issued by an approved warehouse as de­
fined in §  421.5007(b) (1). The receipts 
must be negotiable, must cover eligible 
rice actually in store in the warehouse 
and must clearly indicate whether the 
rice is stored in bulk or in bags (sacks), 
and whether the rice is to be delivered 
in bulk or in bags (sacks). Under the 
uniform rice storage agreement, the 
warehouseman guarantees the quantity 
and quality of the rice unless the ware­
house receipts or accompanying supple­
mental certificates state that the rice 
is stored “identity preserved” or “modi­
fied commingled.” In the case of rice 
stored identity preserved the warehouse­
man is not a guarantor but is required 
to load out the identical rice for which 
the warehouse receipt was issued. In 
the case of rice stored modified com­
mingled, the warehouseman guarantees 
quantity but not quality and the rice 
is stored in one lot, the identity of which 
the warehouseman is required to main­
tain. The warehouse receipts or ac­
companying supplemental certificates 
representing rice stored modified com­
mingled shall contain the following 
statement:
Modified commingled means the storage 
or handling of rice in bulk or in bags by 
com m in gling in one lot rice of a single 
class and of a similar grade and quality, in 
such manner that rice actually deposited 
in that lot prior to a sample being drawn 
for quality determination, and no other, 
may be delivered to the holder of each ware­
house receipt issued with respect to such 
rice.
(b) If the receipt is issued for rice of 
which the warehouseman is the owner 
either solely, jointly, or in common with

Sec. 303. As used in regulations prescribed pursuant to section 
302 hereof, those terms of the said section 402 of title 37 of the 
United States Code which are quoted in the subsections of this section 
shall have the meaning or application stated with respect thereto:
(a) The term “entitled to receive basic pay” shall be considered 
applicable to members while they are on the active list or while they 
are required to perform duty in accordance with law for which they 
are entitled to basic pay: Provided , that such term shall not be 
applicable to any member while absent from duty under conditions 
which, under laws governing the particular service concerned, would 
prevent him from receiving full basic pay.
(b) The term “when rations in kind are not available” shall be 
considered applicable in the case of enlisted members on duty at sta­
tions where it is determined, in accordance with regulations prescribed 
pursuant to section 302 hereof, that it is impracticable for subsist­
ence in kind to be furnished by the United States.
(c) The term “when permission to mess separately is granted” 
shall be considered applicable in the case of enlisted members on duty 
at stations or while sick in hospitals where a mess for subsisting 
enlisted members is available and when such enlisted members are 
authorized to subsist themselves independently. Such term shall also 
be considered applicable in the case of enlisted members during all 
periods of authorized leave, including periods of leave or delay while 
en route between duty stations.
(d) The term “when assigned to duty under emergency conditions 
where no messing facilities of the United States are available” shall 
be considered applicable in the case of enlisted members assigned to 
duty under conditions requiring extraordinary expenses for subsistence 
as determined in accordance with regulations prescribed pursuant to 
section 302 hereof.
(e) The term “being subsisted at the expense of the United States” 
shall be considered applicable to enlisted members who are subsisted 
in kind by the United States and to enlisted members while they are in 
a travel status and are entitled to a per-diem allowance in lieu of 
subsistence or to a mileage allowance.

officer or enlisted members under conditions for which “sea duty” pay

where a member is assigned to duty, or the home yard or the home port 
of a ship in which a member is required to perform duty, under orders

and any station on shore or any receiving ship where a member is as­
signed and in fact occupies, with his dependents, if any, quarters under
- the jurisdiction of any of the uniformed services shall also be deemed 
during such occupancy to be his permanent station: Provided , That in 
the case of members of the National Guard, the Air National Guard 
or reserve components of any of the uniformed services on active duty 
for training, the place where the training duty is being qierformed 
shall be deemed to be the permanent station of such members for the 
purposes of these regulations.
S ec. 402. Except as otherwise by statute heretofore or hereafter 
provided, a member shall be entitled to payment of basic allowances 
for quarters, in accordance with these regulations and any regulations 
prescribed pursuant hereto, during shell time or times as he is entitled 
to receive basic pay.
S ec. 403. Any quarters or housing facilities under the jurisdiction 
of any of the uniformed services in fact occupied without payment of 
rental charges (a) by a member and his dependents, or (b) at his 
permanent station by a member without dependents, or (c) by the 
dependents of a member on field duty or on sea duty or on duty at a 
station where adequate quarters are not available for his dependents, 
shall be deemed to have been assigned to such member as appropriate 
and adequate quarters, and no basic allowance for quarters shall 
accrue to such member under such circumstances unless the occupancy
(i) occurs while such member is in a duty or leave status incident to 
a change of/ permanent station and is of a temporary nature under 
standards prescribed by regulations issued by the Secretary of Defense 
in the case of members of the Army, Navy, Air Force, or Marine 
Corps, and the reserve components thereof, or by the appropriate 
Secretary in the case of members of the other uniformed services, or
(ii) occurs while such member is in a leave status not incident to a 
change of permanent station and does not exceed seven consecutive 
days at one location: Provided , That occupancy of quarters under such 
circumstances for a period in excess of such 7-day period or such other 
temporary period as may be authorized under standards prescribed 
by regulations issued by the Secretary concerned shall not result in 
a forfeiture of basic allowance for quarters for such 7-day or other 
authorized period: Provided further , That this paragraph shall not 
apply to occupancy of quarters as a guest of another member.
S ec. 404. When adequate quarters for his dependents are not avail­
able for assignment at his perfnanent station to a member with de­
pendents, he may occupy quarters of the United States designated for 
members without dependents without affecting his right to receive 
payment of basic allowances for quarters, if permitted or required to 
occupy quarters at such station. Under such circumstances, a member 
may not occupy quarters of the United States which exceed the mini­
mum standards for members of his grade without dependents, as

able (a) exceed the minimum standards, and (b) are made available

assignment as family housing to members of similar rank.

tion 101(5) of title 37 of the United States Code), with respect to per­
sonnel of the uniformed services within their respective departments, 
are hereby authorized to prescribe such supplementary regulations not 
inconsistent herewith as they may deem necessary or desirable for 
carrying out these regulations, and such supplementary regulations 
shall be uniform for all the services to the fullest extent practicable.

mines that military operational conditions require otherwise, a com­
missioned officer without dependents who is in a pay grade above pay 
grade 0 -3  and who is assigned to quarters of the United States or a

priate to his grade or rank and adequate for himself, may elect not to 
occupy those quarters and instead to receive the basic allowance for 
quarters prescribed for his pay grade by section 403 of title 37 of the.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 1 of Executive Order 10892, signed 1960-11-08, amends section 6 of Executive Order 10152 of August 17, 1950 to read as a new text on submarine-duty incentive pay: members attached to an active submarine, including one under construction from the time builders’ trials commence, "shall be entitled to receive incentive pay" for submarine duty, with the same entitlement for operators and crew members of operational self-propelled submersibles and for periods of training and rehabilitation on nuclear-powered submarines. Later event: Executive Order 11120, signed 1963-10-02 and effective as of 1963-10-01, restates section 6 of EO 10152 again ("Section 6 is amended to read as follows") with a rewritten text. Before: entitlement for members attached to an active submarine (including one in builders’ trials) and submersible crews, with nuclear-submarine training and rehabilitation periods as determined by the Secretary of the Navy. After: entitlement as determined by the Secretary of the Navy, extended to members qualified in submarines assigned as prospective crew or under instruction for assignment to a submarine of advanced design, with nuclear training and rehabilitation periods, and submersible crews. The substance of the section changed, which a reviewer should note. Under the owner’s strike-and-insert ruling the clause continues, amended, until the order ends, so the 1963 restatement is a later event and not the first end; the alternative reading, that the 1963 restatement ended this order’s section 6 text on 1963-10-01, is disclosed as an earlier candidate. First end: Executive Order 11157, signed 1964-06-22 (published 1964-06-24), revokes this order by number: its section 502 says "The following Executive orders are revoked:" and lists "Executive Order No. 10892 of November 8,1960." (item (j)) alongside EO 10152 and EO 11120. EO 11157 has no effective-date wording, so the signing date is recorded; the filing date 1964-06-22 and publication date 1964-06-24 are the alternative readings.

research_rationale:
EO 10892 amends EO 10152 on submarine-duty incentive pay with an effective-as-of clause; provisional status no. I read the held registered Federal Register text, confirmed identity and a two-clause inventory (section 1 and section 2). EO 11120 restated the section in 1963 (a later event, with before and after text and a note that the substance changed). EO 11157 (1964-06-22) revokes the order by number and is the first end in held evidence. The machine searches carry no coverage warning and show no hit.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Searched for an end earlier than 1964-06-22. Section 2’s effective-as-of date is not an end. EO 11120 restates section 6 and is a later event with an alternative earlier-candidate reading disclosed; it does not name EO 10892 as revoked or superseded. The Cruden number lookup finds this number cited in EO 11157 and its Federal Register page and in a page listing of EO 10893, and the dossier’s other lead (EO 11120) is a restatement of EO 10152. No other held order ends it.","independent_command_check":"Section 1 has one command (restate section 6 of EO 10152) and section 2 has none after its effective date; neither survives revocation. Whether EO 10152 itself continued is separate, since EO 11157 section 502 also revokes it.","savings_check":"No saving language in EO 11157 (held text searched); pay earned is an accrued effect resting on the pay statute.","scope_check":"Both clauses are covered by the revocation of the whole order in section 502 of EO 11157, which lists EO 10892 by number. The two-clause inventory (section 1 amendment of section 6 of EO 10152; section 2 effective date) is complete for the held text."}

savings_residuals.reason: EO 11157 has no saving or exception clause (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become, except, notwithstanding, hereafter; the only hit is the unrelated words heretofore or hereafter provided in section 402, and there is no effective-date wording). Incentive pay earned for submarine duty while the amended section 6 ran is an accrued effect that rests on the pay statute, not on this order, and does not keep the order operative.

Sec. 303. As used in regulations prescribed pursuant to section 
302 hereof, those terms of the said section 402 of title 37 of the 
United States Code which are quoted in the subsections of this section 
shall have the meaning or application stated with respect thereto:
(a) The term “entitled to receive basic pay” shall be considered 
applicable to members while they are on the active list or while they 
are required to perform duty in accordance with law for which they 
are entitled to basic pay: Provided , that such term shall not be 
applicable to any member while absent from duty under conditions 
which, under laws governing the particular service concerned, would 
prevent him from receiving full basic pay.
(b) The term “when rations in kind are not available” shall be 
considered applicable in the case of enlisted members on duty at sta­
tions where it is determined, in accordance with regulations prescribed 
pursuant to section 302 hereof, that it is impracticable for subsist­
ence in kind to be furnished by the United States.
(c) The term “when permission to mess separately is granted” 
shall be considered applicable in the case of enlisted members on duty 
at stations or while sick in hospitals where a mess for subsisting 
enlisted members is available and when such enlisted members are 
authorized to subsist themselves independently. Such term shall also 
be considered applicable in the case of enlisted members during all 
periods of authorized leave, including periods of leave or delay while 
en route between duty stations.
(d) The term “when assigned to duty under emergency conditions 
where no messing facilities of the United States are available” shall 
be considered applicable in the case of enlisted members assigned to 
duty under conditions requiring extraordinary expenses for subsistence 
as determined in accordance with regulations prescribed pursuant to 
section 302 hereof.
(e) The term “being subsisted at the expense of the United States” 
shall be considered applicable to enlisted members who are subsisted 
in kind by the United States and to enlisted members while they are in 
a travel status and are entitled to a per-diem allowance in lieu of 
subsistence or to a mileage allowance.

of any of the uniformed services in fact occupied without payment of 
rental charges (a) by a member and his dependents, or (b) at his 
permanent station by a member without dependents, or (c) by the 
dependents of a member on field duty or on sea duty or on duty at a 
station where adequate quarters are not available for his dependents,

apply to occupancy of quarters as a guest of another member.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Executive Order 10904, signed 1961-01-12, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between carriers represented by the New York Harbor Carriers’ Conference Committee and certain of their employees. Its single paragraph carries three commands that belong to one procedure: creation of the board ("hereby create a board of"), the direction that the board report to the President ("within thirty days from the date"), and the status-quo rule that, from the order’s date and for thirty days after the report, no change in the conditions out of which the dispute arose is to be made except by agreement ("except by agreement"). The order has no termination clause, fixed end date or revocation clause of its own. The thirty-day report date and the end of the thirty-day period after the report are spent facts and not ends. The held NMB report text for this board (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10904_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10904_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_3afb8d1c9a.txt) gives the date 1961-03-06 on its cover and letter of transmittal; a dated transmittal letter is not proof of the day the President received the report, so this is a disclosed spent fact and not an end. If the report was made on 1961-03-06, the thirty-day period after the report ran through 1961-04-05, and the order was functionally spent on 1961-04-05 (owner ruling research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-report-deadline.md, both dates recorded). First end: Executive Order 12553, signed 1986-02-25, revokes this order by number. The cited source is the enacting sentence of EO 12553, which says "longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" The dossier records an agent-located acting provision for this pair that an independent AI review upheld (a hypothesis, not a certification). The table in EO 12553 (page 11 of the held Federal Register text) lists the number 10904 at character offset 10765 as entry 63 of 64; the text layer prints the 64 numbers first and the 64 subjects afterwards, and entry 63 of the subject list is the subject Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute, which agrees with this order’s own title. The alignment is by position, not by a printed row, and a reviewer should confirm it. EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording of its own (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become and similar words), so the date it was signed, 1986-02-25, is recorded as the end date. The held text also shows the filing date 1986-02-26 and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03; those are the alternative readings and none of them changes the conclusion that the order was no longer in force after 1986-03-03.

Executive Order 10904
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD  
TO INVESTIGATE A DISPUTE BE­
TWEEN CERTAIN CARRIERS REP­
RESENTED BY THE NEW YORK  
HARBOR CARRIERS’ CONFERENCE  
COMMITTEE AND CERTAIN OF  
THEIR EMPLOYEES
WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
certain carriers represented by the New 
York Harbor Carriers’  Conference Com­
mittee, designated in the List of Carriers 
attached hereto and hereby made a part 
hereof, and certain of their employees 
represented by the Lighter Captains’  
Union, Local 996, I.L.A., a labor organi­
zation; and
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provisions 
of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; 
and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as to 
deprive a section of the country of es­
sential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U.S.C. 160) , I hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, 
to investigate this dispute. No member 
of the board shall be pecuniarily or 
otherwise interested in any organization 
of railroad employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the dispute 
within thirty days from the date of this 
order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by carriers represented by the 
New York Harbor Carriers’ Conference 
Committee, or by their employees, in the 
conditions out of which the dispute arose.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Executive Order 10944, signed 1961-05-19, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between the Baltimore and Ohio Railroad Company and other carriers and certain of their employees. Its single paragraph carries three commands that belong to one procedure: creation of the board ("hereby create a board of"), the direction that the board report to the President ("within thirty days from the date"), and the status-quo rule that, from the order’s date and for thirty days after the report, no change in the conditions out of which the dispute arose is to be made except by agreement ("no change, except by agreement"). The order has no termination clause, fixed end date or revocation clause of its own. The thirty-day report date and the end of the thirty-day period after the report are spent facts and not ends. The held NMB report text for this board (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10944_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10944_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_4ff16ec669.txt) gives the date 1961-07-10 on its cover and letter of transmittal; a dated transmittal letter is not proof of the day the President received the report, so this is a disclosed spent fact and not an end. If the report was made on 1961-07-10, the thirty-day period after the report ran through 1961-08-09, and the order was functionally spent on 1961-08-09 (owner ruling research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-report-deadline.md, both dates recorded). First end: Executive Order 12553, signed 1986-02-25, revokes this order by number. The cited source is the enacting sentence of EO 12553, which says "longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" The dossier records an agent-located acting provision for this pair that an independent AI review upheld (a hypothesis, not a certification). The table in EO 12553 (page 12 of the held Federal Register text, outside the cited enacting sentence) lists this order on its own row beginning at character offset 16081: the number 10944 followed by the subject Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute, which agrees with this order’s own title. EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording of its own (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become and similar words), so the date it was signed, 1986-02-25, is recorded as the end date. The held text also shows the filing date 1986-02-26 and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03; those are the alternative readings and none of them changes the conclusion that the order was no longer in force after 1986-03-03.

Executive Order 10944
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD  
TO INVESTIGATE A DISPUTE BE­
TWEEN THE BALTIMORE AND OHIO  
RAILROAD COMPANY AND OTHER  
CARRIERS AND CERTAIN OF THEIR  
EMPLOYEES
WHEREAS a dispute exists between  
the Baltimore and Ohio Railroad Com­
pany and other carriers represented by  
the Eastern, Western, and Southeastern  
Carriers’  Conference Committees, desig­
nated in List A attached hereto and  
hereby made a part hereof,, and certain  
of their employees represented by the  
Railroad Yardmasters of America, a  
labor organization;  and 
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provi­
sions of the Railway Labor Act as  
amended; and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board,  
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as  
to deprive a section of the country of  
essential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the  
authority vested in me by section 10 of  
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45  
U.S.C. 160), I hereby create a board of  
three members, to be appointed by me,  
to investigate this dispute. No member  
of the board shall be pecuniarily or  
otherwise interested in any organization  
of railroad employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to  
the President with respect to the dispute  
within thirty days from the date of this  
order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this  
date and for thirty days after the board  
has made its report to the President,  
no change, except by agreement, shall  
be made by the Baltimore and Ohio Rail­
road Company and other carriers repre­
sented by the Eastern, Western, and  
Southeastern Carriers’  Conference Com­
mittees, or by their employees, in the  
conditions out of which the dispute arose.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Executive Order 10949, signed 1961-06-26, creates a Board of Inquiry under section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act, 1947, directs it to report to the President "on or before" June 30, 1961, and provides that after its report the board continues in existence until "terminated by the President". Three commands result: creation of the board, the report deadline, and continued existence until presidential termination. Later event: Executive Order 10951, signed 1961-06-29, extends until 9 a.m., July 3, 1961 the time within which this board must report (inclusive reading; the exclusive reading is that it ends when that moment begins). The extension is a later event with its own quote, and an extended report deadline is not an end (owner rulings 2026-10-21 until-dates and report deadline). The only own-terms end is termination by the President. No held text records one: a held-corpus regular-expression search for a board of inquiry being terminated returned no match, and no held text gives the date the board reported. That absence is not proof that no termination occurred, so it is disclosed as an open earlier-end candidate; the held evidence does not show an earlier end, and under the owner’s report-deadline ruling the order ends on its express revocation. First end: Executive Order 12553, signed 1986-02-25, revokes this order by number; its enacting sentence (outside the cited span) revokes the listed orders and any amendments to them, and the cited span, page 12 of the held text, lists the order on its own row, "10949 Creating a board of inquiry to report on a labor dispute affecting the maritime industry", beginning at character offset 16156; the same table lists EO 10951, the amendment. EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording of its own (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become and similar words), so the date it was signed, 1986-02-25, is recorded as the end date. The held text also shows the filing date 1986-02-26 and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03; those are the alternative readings and none of them changes the conclusion that the order was no longer in force after 1986-03-03.

Executive Order 10949
CREATING A BOARD OF INQUIRY TO
REPORT ON A LABOR DISPUTE AF­
FECTING THE MARITIME INDUSTRY
OF THE UNITED STATES
WHEREAS, there exists a labor dispute 
between certain ship owners and opera­
tors in the United States foreign and  
domestic trades and certain of their em­
ployees represented by: the National  
Maritime Union of America; the Sea­
farers International Union of North  
America; the National Marine Engineers’  
Beneficial Association; the International  
Organization of Masters, Mates and Pi­
lots; the American Radio Association;  
the Radio Officers Union; the Staff Of­
ficers Association of America; and
WHEREAS, such dispute has resulted  
in a strike which, in my opinion, affects  
a substantial part of the maritime in­
dustry, an industry engaged in trade,  
commerce, and transportation among  
the several States and with foreign na­
tions; and which strike will, if permitted  
to continue, imperil the national health  
and safety:
NOW THEREFORE, by virtue of the  
authority vested in me by section 206 of  
the Labor-Management Relations Act,  
*  1947, 61 Stat. 155 <29 U.S.C. 176), I  
hereby create a Board of Inquiry con­
sisting of The Honorable David L. Cole,  
Chairman, Judge Samuel I. Rosenman,  
and Professor James J. Healy as mem­
bers to inquire into the issues involved  
in such dispute.
The Board shall have powers and  
duties as set forth in Title II of such  
Act. The Board shall report to the Pres­
ident in accordance with the provisions  
of section 206 of such Act on or before  
June 30,1961.
Upon submission of its report, the  
Board shall continue in existence to per­
form such'  other functions as may be  
required under such Act, until the Board  
is terminated by the President.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Executive Order 10951, signed 1961-06-29, is a one-sentence order under section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act, 1947. It commands one thing: it extends the time within which the board of inquiry created by Executive Order 10949 must report to the President ("I hereby extend until" 9 a.m., July 3, 1961). That is a report deadline, recorded inclusively as running through 9 a.m. on 1961-07-03, with the exclusive reading (the extension ends when that moment begins) as the alternative; it is a deadline and a later event of EO 10949, and it is not an end (owner rulings 2026-10-21 until-dates and report deadline). The order has no termination clause of its own, and no held text gives the date on which the board actually reported, so the order was functionally spent no later than 1961-07-03 only if the board reported by then, which the held evidence does not establish. First end: Executive Order 12553, signed 1986-02-25, revokes this order by number. The cited source is the enacting sentence of EO 12553, which says "longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" The dossier records an agent-located acting provision for this pair that an independent AI review upheld (a hypothesis, not a certification). The table in EO 12553 (page 12 of the held Federal Register text, outside the cited enacting sentence) lists this order on its own row beginning at character offset 16252: the number 10951 followed by the subject Amending Executive Order No. 10949 creating a board of inquiry to report on a labor dispute affecting, which agrees with this order’s own title. EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording of its own (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become and similar words), so the date it was signed, 1986-02-25, is recorded as the end date. The held text also shows the filing date 1986-02-26 and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03; those are the alternative readings and none of them changes the conclusion that the order was no longer in force after 1986-03-03.

EO 10951 extends the report time of the EO 10949 board of inquiry; provisional status no. I read the held registered Federal Register text, confirmed identity from heading and number, and confirmed a single-clause inventory (the one-sentence extension). The three machine searches carry no coverage warning and show no contrary hit.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Executive Order 10954, signed 1961-07-26, amends the last paragraph of Executive Order 10906 (inspection of certain tax returns) "amended to read as follows:" a paragraph that makes EO 10906 effective on its filing for publication and supersedes EO 10738 of November 15, 1957 as to inspection by State tax officials of estate and gift-tax returns made under the Internal Revenue Code of 1954; the order’s closing sentence makes it effective as of January 18, 1961. The order is one amendatory command whose substance is the restated effective-date and supersession paragraph. First end: Executive Order 12553, signed 1986-02-25, revokes EO 10906 and amendments to it, and names this order by number. The dossier holds no located acting-provision record for this pair, so the cited source is the whole held Federal Register text of EO 12553 (the dossier’s actor context). Its enacting sentence says "longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and its page-12 table lists this order on its own row, "10954 Amending an authorization to inspect certain tax returns", beginning at character offset 16457; the same table lists EO 10906 as the last entry of the page-11 list and EO 10738 as entry 42 of that list. Because EO 10954 is named by number, the owner’s unnamed-instruments rule is not needed to reach it. EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording of its own (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become and similar words), so the date it was signed, 1986-02-25, is recorded as the end date. The held text also shows the filing date 1986-02-26 and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03; those are the alternative readings and none of them changes the conclusion that the order was no longer in force after 1986-03-03.

EO 10954 amends the last paragraph of EO 10906 on inspection of tax returns; provisional status no. I read the held registered Federal Register text, confirmed identity, and confirmed a single-clause inventory. EO 12553 (1986-02-25) lists EO 10954 by number and revokes the listed orders and any amendments; it is the first end in held evidence. The dossier’s missing lines (no located provision for EO 10738 and EO 12553) are resolved by reading the held texts: EO 10738 is the order EO 10954 supersedes in part, and EO 12553 lists it too.

A statute rewriting 26 U.S.C. 6103 that does not name the order would not end it (owner ruling 2026-10-21 unnamed instruments), and no held statute text is cited as an end. savings_residuals.reason: EO 12553 has no saving, exception or pending-matters language: a search of the whole held text for except, notwithstanding, nothing in, saving, pending and similar words found only incidental uses inside other orders’ subject lines. The supersession of EO 10738 as to State tax officials was a one-time effect that took hold in 1961 and is moot because EO 12553 revokes EO 10738 as well; whether State officials may now inspect such returns depends on the Internal Revenue Code and its regulations, not on this order.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Executive Order 10963, signed 1961-09-01, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between the Pullman Company and the Chicago, Milwaukee, St. Paul & Pacific Railroad Company and certain of their employees. Its single paragraph carries three commands that belong to one procedure: creation of the board ("hereby create a board of"), the direction that the board report to the President ("within thirty days from the date"), and the status-quo rule that, from the order’s date and for thirty days after the report, no change in the conditions out of which the dispute arose is to be made except by agreement ("except by agreement"). The order has no termination clause, fixed end date or revocation clause of its own. The thirty-day report date and the end of the thirty-day period after the report are spent facts and not ends. The held NMB report text for this board (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10963_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10963_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_a3eb3dd50c.txt) gives the date 1961-12-11 on its cover and letter of transmittal; a dated transmittal letter is not proof of the day the President received the report, so this is a disclosed spent fact and not an end. If the report was made on 1961-12-11, the thirty-day period after the report ran through 1962-01-10, and the order was functionally spent on 1962-01-10 (owner ruling research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-report-deadline.md, both dates recorded). First end: Executive Order 12553, signed 1986-02-25, revokes this order by number. The cited source is the enacting sentence of EO 12553, which says "longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" The dossier records an agent-located acting provision for this pair that an independent AI review upheld (a hypothesis, not a certification). The table in EO 12553 (page 12 of the held Federal Register text, outside the cited enacting sentence) lists this order on its own row beginning at character offset 16624: the number 10963 followed by the subject Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes, which agrees with this order’s own title. EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording of its own (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become and similar words), so the date it was signed, 1986-02-25, is recorded as the end date. The held text also shows the filing date 1986-02-26 and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03; those are the alternative readings and none of them changes the conclusion that the order was no longer in force after 1986-03-03.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Executive Order 10963
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD  
TO INVESTIGATE DISPUTES BE­
TWEEN THE PULLMAN COMPANY  
AND THE CHICAGO, MILWAUKEE,  
ST. PAUL &  PACIFIC RAILROAD  
COMPANY AND CERTAIN OF THEIR  
EMPLOYEES
WHEREAS disputes exist between the  
Pullman Company and the Chicago,  
Milwaukee, St. Paul &  Pacific Railroad  
Company, carriers, and certain of their  
employees represented by the Order of  
Railway Conductors and Brakemen, a  
labor organization; and  
WHEREAS these disputes have not  
heretofore been adjusted under the pro­
visions of the Railway Labor Act, as  
amended; and
WHEREAS these disputes, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board,  
threaten substantially to interrupt inter­
state commerce to a degree such as to  
deprive a section of the country of  
essential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the  
authority vested in me by section 10 of  
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45  
U.S.C. 160), I hereby create a board of  
three members, to be appointed by me,  
to investigate these disputes. No mem­
ber of the board shall be pecuniarily or  
otherwise interested in any organization  
of railroad employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to  
the President with respect to these dis­
putes within thirty days from the date  
of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this  
date and for thirty days after the board  
has made its report to the President, no  
change, except by agreement, shall be  
made by the Pullman Company and the  
Chicago, Milwaukee, St. Paul &  Pacific  
Railroad Company, or by their em­
ployees, in the conditions out of which  
these disputes arose.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Executive Order 10971, signed 1961-11-01, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between Trans World Airlines, Inc., and certain of its employees. Its single paragraph carries three commands that belong to one procedure: creation of the board ("hereby create a board of"), the direction that the board report to the President ("within thirty days from the date"), and the status-quo rule that, from the order’s date and for thirty days after the report, no change in the conditions out of which the dispute arose is to be made except by agreement ("except by agreement"). The order has no termination clause, fixed end date or revocation clause of its own. The thirty-day report date and the end of the thirty-day period after the report are spent facts and not ends. No held text gives the actual date of this board’s report, so neither the report date nor the end of the thirty-day period after it is established from held evidence; the claim does not depend on them because a report deadline and a status-quo period are not ends (owner ruling research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-report-deadline.md). First end: Executive Order 12553, signed 1986-02-25, revokes this order by number. The cited source is the enacting sentence of EO 12553, which says "longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" The dossier records an agent-located acting provision for this pair that an independent AI review upheld (a hypothesis, not a certification). The table in EO 12553 (page 12 of the held Federal Register text, outside the cited enacting sentence) lists this order on its own row beginning at character offset 16845: the number 10971 followed by the subject Creating an emergency board to investigate an airline labor dispute, which agrees with this order’s own title. EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording of its own (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become and similar words), so the date it was signed, 1986-02-25, is recorded as the end date. The held text also shows the filing date 1986-02-26 and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03; those are the alternative readings and none of them changes the conclusion that the order was no longer in force after 1986-03-03.

plicable regulations for the farm for

would be impaired.

are hereby designated as areas of recur­

through November 30, both inclusive, of 
each year, and such States are hereby 
designated as areas of seasonal infesta­

screwworms currently exist in Alabama 
and Georgia, and such States are hereby 
designated as areas of temporary infes­
